10	
11	A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:
12	
13	```
14	cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
15	  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
16	  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
17	  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
18	  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
19	```
20	
21	The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
22	without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
23	RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
24	reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
25	[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].
26	
27	FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
28	does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
29	(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
30	them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
31	created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
32	shown; web-view crashes vanish).
33	
34	`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
35	not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
36	--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
37	/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.
38	
39	CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
40	repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
41	`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
42	worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
43	"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
44	`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
45	absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
46	stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
47	(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
48	`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
49	paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

2	name: subagent-worktrees-create-manually
3	description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: feedback

8	  modified: 2026-09-08T16:33:59.964Z
9	---
10	
11	On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
12	worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
13	branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
14	was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
15	was the only option.
16	
17	**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
18	And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
19	"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.
20	
21	**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
22	give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
23	HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
24	so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
25	`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
26	minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
27	fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
28	See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

2	name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
3	description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
8	  modified: 2026-09-18T23:28:33.951Z
9	---
10	
11	Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.
12	
13	**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.
14	
15	The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.
16	
17	**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.
18	
19	**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].
20	
21	**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
22	2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
23	`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
24	`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
25	app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
26	a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
27	on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
28	the harness had opened on the Acer.
29	
30	Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
31	(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
32	captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
33	not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
34	"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.
35	
36	The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
37	read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
38	and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
39	evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
40	being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
41	concluding anything about the app.
42	
43	**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
44	`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
45	(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
46	`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
47	the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.
48	
49	**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
50	`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
51	`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
52	all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
53	directory — the directory alone is not enough.
54	
55	**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.
56	
57	**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.
58	
59	**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
60	against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
61	first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
62	agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
63	had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
64	`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
65	all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
66	treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
67	`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
68	rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.
69	
70	**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
71	"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
72	reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
73	display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
74	sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
75	button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
76	until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].
